channel.title: The Open Archive
channel.description: Essays on maths and science, and write-ups of the projects he builds, by Lanchenba Mutum. Free to read online, with PDFs on request.

item.title: MetaProof: Evidence-Based Authenticity Analysis for Images
item.description: The full write-up of MetaProof, a web app I built that checks an image's metadata, file structure, C2PA Content Credentials, hidden watermarks and pixels, then explains whether it is likely authentic, edited, AI-generated or inconclusive. “Wrongly calling a real photo fake is the costlier mistake. So missing data is never held against a file, the detector's score only decides a verdict on its own when it is very high, signed proof (C2PA) outranks statistical guesses, and when the evidence is weak the answer is inconclusive.”

item.title: Mathematics Behind Jujutsu Kaisen: Gojo Satoru's Infinity
item.description: An examination of Zeno's paradox, convergent series and limits through the 'Infinity' technique of Gojo Satoru in Jujutsu Kaisen. “Between any attacker and Gojo, there is always a distance. That distance can be halved, then halved again, then again, forever. No matter how fast the attack travels, it must first cross half the remaining distance, then half of that, then half of that, an infinite sequence of steps that, Gojo claims, can never be completed.”

item.title: A Tale of Two Infinities
item.description: An introduction to Cantor's discovery that infinite sets can differ in size, and to the distinction between countable and uncountable infinity. “Numbers, our whole world is dominated by numbers, all of which are finite – even if some are simply too large to comprehend. However, there is one “number” which defies all others: infinity.”

item.title: 0.999… = 1: A Paradox That Isn't
item.description: A careful demonstration that 0.999… is exactly equal to 1, with an explanation of why the result so often surprises students. “This shows that the infinite sum represented by 0.999… is exactly equal to 1. It does not merely approach 1—it reaches it in a precise mathematical sense.”

item.title: A Proof for the Unprovable
item.description: An account of Hilbert's programme and Gödel's incompleteness theorems, which showed that not every mathematical truth can be proved. “Let me break a rule, mathematics can't prove everything…”

item.title: A Mathematical Glitch in the Fourth Wall
item.description: An exploration of the number 73, from a well-known television reference to the proof by Pomerance and Spicer of its unique properties. “A journey through the improbable mathematics of 73. From a sitcom gag to a rigorous proof by Pomerance and Spicer, this essay explores why a single prime number stands unique in the infinite sea of integers, explained for curious minds.”

item.title: 'Tis the Season: A Mathematical Foray into Secret Santa
item.description: An analysis of the probability that a participant draws their own name in Secret Santa, introducing derangements and the unexpected appearance of e. “In this essay, we’ll explore the mathematics behind why the way we usually play this game is the stuff of nightmares.”

item.title: AI Is Fundamentally Unintelligent
item.description: A study of why leading AI models answer a simple conditional-probability question incorrectly, and what this reveals about their reasoning. “Nowadays, AI is considered to be a near-flawless calculator capable of solving any question. Yet, a simple probability question can highlight a surprising weakness.”

item.title: A Prisoner's Dilemma
item.description: An introduction to game theory through the Prisoner's Dilemma, examining rational choice when both cooperation and betrayal are possible. “In Game Theory, one of the most important thought experiments is the Prisoner’s Dilemma. It entails two rational agents who have been arrested and are being interrogated separately (i.e., communication is not allowed between them).”

item.title: A Deep Dive into the Possibilities of LEGO
item.description: A combinatorial investigation into the number of ways in which a small set of LEGO bricks can be combined. “LEGO. It's such a simple childhood toy that I have played with from a very young age, and I'm sure most of the people reading this would have as well. However, most don't realise how much maths can be behind such a simple plastic block.”

item.title: A Voyage to the Planet of Fractal Geometry
item.description: An illustrated journey through the branches of geometry, culminating in fractals: self-similar shapes with non-integer dimensions. “Welcome to the solar system of geometry created by our father of geometry, known as Euclid. In the vast universe of mathematics, the solar system of geometry stands as the most notable and elegant solar system.”

item.title: How Do Patterns in Nature Relate to Mathematical Laws?
item.description: An examination of Alan Turing's work on morphogenesis, showing how the spots and stripes of animal markings arise from reaction–diffusion between activators and inhibitors. “Many people associate Alan Turing with the Enigma machine, but in this essay, I shall be exploring one of his later works where he discovered the connection between nature and mathematics.”

item.title: Absolute Cinema of Math
item.description: An exploration of the mathematics underlying music, from the physics of vibrating strings to harmonics and the equation of a wave. “Hearing the heartbreaking melody gives you goosebumps, you might wonder why? Well, math is the answer.”
